## Observed Facts

**Count:** 20,217 BGL Log Entries contain "ciod" between 2005-06-01 (inclusive) and 2005-07-01 (exclusive). Matching is case-insensitive substring on the message. By component: APP 13,409, KERNEL 6,803, MMCS 5 [E1].

**First matching entry:** line 4988, 2005-06-03 16:17:40.190183, node R26-M0-NC-I:J18-U11, APP, FATAL [E2]:
`ciod: Error loading /p/gb2/stella/RAPTOR/65641/raptor: invalid or missing program image, No such file or directory`

**Just before (lines 4978–4987) [E3]:**
- 4978–4983 (KERNEL, INFO, node R16-M1-N2-C:J17-U01, 16:12:35–16:12:36): correctable DDR memory errors, "CE sym 2 …", ending with "total of 31 ddr error(s) detected and corrected".
- 4984–4987 (KERNEL, INFO, nodes in R22-M0, 16:16:26): "generating core.257", "core.385", "core.65", "core.1". These are core-dump messages from other nodes.
- None of the ten preceding lines mention ciod.

**Just after (lines 4989–4998) [E3]:** the same FATAL ciod error repeats on a series of I/O nodes within about 0.3 seconds: R26-M0-NC, R26-M0-N8, R26-M0-N4, R26-M0-N0 (J18), then R27-M1-NC and R27-M1-N8. Each line has the same program path, `/p/gb2/stella/RAPTOR/65641/raptor`.

## Hypotheses

- The most likely cause is that the job's executable (`/p/gb2/stella/RAPTOR/65641/raptor`) was missing or not readable on the shared file system when the job was launched. The error is "No such file or directory" on every node, so the file was probably absent, not corrupt. This fits the burst of identical errors across nodes.
- The KERNEL core-dump lines just before (16:16:26) come from a different job or from earlier failures. They are not confirmed as the cause of the ciod error.

## Unknowns

- The logs do not show why the file was missing (a bad path, a deleted or moved build, or a file-system outage).
- I did not check what happened after line 4998. I have not confirmed whether this burst ended, whether the job was retried, or whether the errors recurred later in June.
- I did not check whether the 20,217 matches are mostly this same message. Only the first 10 lines of the sequence have been looked at.
- The count includes any message containing "ciod" as a substring, not only ciod error messages.

## Next Step

Run a count of this exact error across the same window to see how much of the 20,217 it accounts for and when it stops:
`count_by` on BGL, group_by `node`, query `invalid or missing program image`, start 2005-06-01, end 2005-07-01. Then run `trend` with bucket `hour` on the same query, starting from 2005-06-03, to see whether the burst is a single event or repeats.
